Politics · Conflict

Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says

Global · Major · New

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

The White House announced that US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen next week. The discussion is expected to focus on nuclear weapons reduction, with Iran potentially included, while Ukraine is not expected to be on the agenda. No agreement is anticipated from the talks, and Moscow and Beijing have not yet commented.

Why it matters

The meeting occurs after the US-Russia nuclear weapons control treaty expired in February, leaving major nuclear arsenals without significant guardrails. Trump aims to replace the deal with a new agreement including China, though analysts suggest such cooperation could take years.

Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely'

Global · Major · Updated

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

US President Donald Trump stated that renewed US attacks on Iran are "highly unlikely" and described Iran as "militarily is effectively over" following a meeting with the Qatari prime minister. He indicated the US is maintaining the status quo at the behest of neighboring countries, while noting that global oil prices dipped further after his comments.

Why it matters

Trump's remarks follow midterm election results that Republican figures blamed on the Iran war, and he has hinted at de-escalation while maintaining a naval blockade to protect Gulf allies.

Anthropic heads for $1.3 trillion valuation in major stock market listing

Global · Major · Updated

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

Anthropic will list on the Nasdaq on November 19, offering 825 million shares at a price range of $70 to $78 each. The company expects to raise between $57.75 billion and $64.35 billion from the sale of new shares, with total net proceeds estimated between $84.6 billion and $93.7 billion including a private placement to major tech firms.

The findings indicate that primordial interstellar ice is a common ingredient in planetary systems, implying that the raw materials for water-rich, potentially habitable worlds may be widespread.

PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery

Global · Major · Previously featured

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

Physical Superintelligence (PSI) used Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model to solve the 18-year-old Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, a central open problem in quantum query complexity. The proof, autoformalized in Lean, indicates that quantum computers cannot solve certain difficult problems faster than classical ones via that specific avenue. PSI currently generates revenue by optimizing data centers but aims to convert theoretical physics breakthroughs into technologies, acknowledging that validating AI-generated results in the physical world remains a significant challenge.

Why it matters

The event highlights a shift in scientific discovery where AI models solve complex theoretical problems, prompting the academic community to develop new standards for verification and transparency as 'neolabs' emerge.

Daily News

Science

The amazing disappearing exoplanet

Global · Major · Catch up

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

Researchers reported that the hot Jupiter exoplanet TOI-2535b has stopped transiting its host star after seven years of regular observations. The disappearance is attributed to gravitational interactions with an unseen companion planet orbiting in a different plane, which altered TOI-2535b's orbital inclination. Simulations suggest the unseen planet is at least Saturn-sized, with about two-thirds of the best-fit models becoming unstable over a million-year timescale.

Why it matters

This is the fastest observed rate of inclination change for an exoplanet orbiting a single star, providing rare insight into the dynamical evolution and potential instability of multi-planet systems.

Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery

Global · Notable · Previously featured

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

Physicists used shot noise measurements to show that electron pairing in cuprate superconductors occurs at the pseudogap energy, supporting the theory that pre-formed pairs exist before superconductivity. The study, published in Science, found that pairing is associated with the pseudogap, ruling out the hypothesis that it arises solely from frozen electron patterns, though it does not exclude intertwined mechanisms.

Why it matters

The findings suggest that the bottleneck for higher-temperature superconductivity in cuprates is achieving phase coherence among pre-formed pairs, rather than forming the pairs themselves, which could guide future material design efforts.

Why it matters

The case highlights a gap in international wildlife regulations, which lack clear processes for facilitating social introductions to rehabilitate traumatized captive apes, potentially limiting their recovery and suitability for future release.

In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits

Sri Lanka · Useful · New

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

A 12-year study of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka found that steady population losses cause social communities to fracture rather than simply shrink. As deaths and departures outpaced newcomers, social networks became smaller, more numerous, and more isolated, with key individuals lost who previously held subgroups together. The researchers linked this social breakdown to habitat degradation and reduced forage, noting that the park's elephant population is now declining faster than predicted.

Why it matters

The study identifies early warning signals, such as network flickering, that could allow conservationists to intervene before populations collapse. It highlights that effective management requires addressing landscape-level threats like human conflict and habitat loss, not just protected area boundaries.

Fund hopes to bring life back to Wellington hospitality

NZ · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

The family of late Lido Cafe owner David George established the Lido Trailblazer Fund to support Wellington's hospitality industry. The fund awards one professional annually $12,500 to travel or train overseas, aiming to bring back innovative ideas and retain emerging talent. Applications are open until 11 December, with the winner to be announced in February.

Why it matters

The fund addresses the ongoing challenges in Wellington's hospitality sector by encouraging independent thinkers to pursue adventurous experiences that could evolve the city's food culture.

Restaurant chains refocus on food quality to bring back diners

Global · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

Major restaurant chains including Wendy's, Burger King, and McDonald's are prioritizing food quality improvements to reverse declining sales and win back diners. Wendy's reported its seventh consecutive quarter of same-store sales declines and rejected a $1.4 billion takeover bid, citing its turnaround strategy. Burger King saw U.S. same-store sales jump 8.4% after menu revamps, while McDonald's is testing new chicken items and coffee upgrades to address recent U.S. sales stagnation.

Why it matters

Industry leaders argue that improving product quality is essential for long-term growth and franchisee profitability, as discounts alone are insufficient to sustain traffic in a market where consumers have become more selective.

How GM is trying to talk used car shoppers into buying new vehicles

United States · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

General Motors revamped its certified used vehicle program as CarBravo, an online portal for multi-brand certified cars, to compete with digital retailers. GM targets 250,000 sales in 2026 and reports that 38% of used-car shoppers convert to new vehicle purchases. Ford and Toyota also operate similar certified preowned programs, with Toyota reporting a 40% conversion rate to new cars.

Why it matters

The strategy leverages longer-term loan options on new cars to make monthly payments comparable to used vehicles, while generating service revenue and subscription sales for dealerships.

Phota Labs, an a16z-backed startup, launched a free iOS app that uses AI to transform everyday photos into professional-looking images while preserving the subjects' identities. The app, founded by former Adobe employees, offers various photography styles and includes invisible watermarks to identify AI-altered images. Why it matters

Goodyear Tire CEO Mark Stewart steps down as company continues turnaround plan

Global · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. announced that CEO Mark Stewart is stepping down effective immediately, with board member Roger Wood serving as interim CEO and president. The leadership change occurs during a multiyear turnaround plan, following third-quarter results showing net sales down 2.3% year over year and an adjusted net loss of $31 million. The company failed to reach its 10% operating margin target for the end of last year and faces headwinds from tariffs, raw material costs, and competition from China.

Why it matters

The board initiated a strategic review to optimize the business mix and footprint, aiming to accelerate progress and capture additional opportunity amid ongoing financial challenges.
